summary: Compiles the issues found with the Stream Control Transmission Protocol since RFC 4960 was published in 2007, together with suggested fixes. It is organized in time order as a list of changes to that text. It is informational and was replaced by RFC 9260.

plainLanguage.summary: A list of mistakes and unclear spots people found in an older rulebook for a data delivery system, along with fixes, written down in the order they were found.

subtitle: A compilation of corrections and clarifications to the Stream Control Transmission Protocol.

tldr.problem: RFC 4960 (SCTP) published in 2007 had ambiguities, errors and implementation issues discovered over more than a decade of use.
tldr.mechanism: This document compiles 50 errata and issues found through implementation experience, testing and discussion, organized in chronological order. Each issue includes a description of the problem, the original text, corrected text, and an explanation of the solution.
tldr.outcome: The fixes were incorporated into RFC 9260, which superseded RFC 4960 as the authoritative SCTP specification. This document serves as a historical record of the changes.

today: RFC 8540 is Informational and has been obsoleted by RFC 9260, published in September 2022. RFC 9260 is the current authoritative SCTP specification and incorporates all the fixes and clarifications from this errata document.

sections.title: Introduction to the SCTP Errata
sections.content:
RFC 4960 defined the Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP) when it was published in September 2007. Since then, implementers, testers and protocol developers using SCTP found problems: some were editorial typos, others were ambiguities that led to different implementations, and some were technical errors in the algorithms and rules the RFC specified.

This document is a companion to RFC 4960. It compiles all the defects found up to February 2019 in the form of a list of 50 corrections. Each correction shows the original text from RFC 4960, the corrected text that should replace it, and an explanation of the problem and solution. This allows implementers to understand what was intended, and provides a historical record of the changes that would eventually become RFC 9260.
sections.plainLanguage: This is a companion document that lists 50 mistakes and confusing parts found in the original SCTP rulebook. Each one shows what the old text said, what it should say, and why.

sections.title: Types of Corrections
sections.content:
The 50 issues in this document fall into several categories:

Congestion Control and Data Transmission: Many issues concern the algorithms that control how fast a sender transmits data. These include the cwnd (congestion window) and ssthresh (slow-start threshold) variables, the handling of Max.Burst, retransmission timeout calculations (RTO), and the notion of flightsize and outstanding data.

State Management and Association Setup: Other issues cover how associations are established and torn down, including the handling of different timer states (T1-init, T1-cookie), cookie handling, endpoint failure detection, and the association error counter. Some clarifications deal with which timer should be used in which state.

Chunk and Message Handling: Several issues address the processing of SCTP chunks (the units that carry control and data messages), including rules for bundling chunks together, the order in which chunks should be processed, and when to send SACK chunks in reply to received data.

Parameters and Protocol Configuration: Issues also cover SCTP protocol parameters (like heartbeat intervals, recommended values for timers and limits), and the registration of new chunk types and parameter types. One change lowered the initial retransmission timeout from 3 seconds to 1 second to align with TCP.

Clarifications and Editorial Fixes: Some issues are simple typos or formatting problems (like a table with incorrect line breaks), while others clarify ambiguous wording or remove undefined terms from the API specification.
sections.plainLanguage: The fixes fall into groups: how fast to send data, how to set up and close connections, how to handle the packets sent back and forth, what settings to use, and fixes to typos or unclear wording.

sections.title: Using the Errata: Structure and Key Corrections
sections.content:
This document is structured to be used alongside RFC 4960. Each issue is given a number (3.1 through 3.50) and includes: a description of the problem (with the original Errata ID if applicable), the problematic text from RFC 4960, the corrected text to substitute, and an explanation of the correction.

Some text was updated multiple times as implementation experience revealed further corrections. The document notes these cases and readers should apply the last delta listed for any multiply-updated text.

The document addresses both subtle and obvious problems. Section 3.1 resolves whether the Path.Max.Retrans threshold is triggered when an error counter reaches or exceeds it. Section 3.6 fixes a bug where the association error counter could wrongly close an association when the currently-used path was alive but idle. Section 3.30 defines key terms like outstanding data, flightsize, and data in flight that the original RFC used but did not define. Section 3.31 clarifies that the Max.Burst limit should not permanently change cwnd.
sections.plainLanguage: Each issue shows what was wrong, what the new text should be, and explains why. Some errors appear more than once in the document, and you need to use the last correction listed.

sections.title: Scope and Coverage
sections.content:
This document clarifies RFC 4960's existing specification without introducing new features or changing the fundamental SCTP design. Small but critical corrections improve interoperability: for instance, Section 3.8 corrects a diagram showing the wrong timer (T1-init instead of T1-cookie) in the cookie-echo state.

Some corrections integrate related RFCs that updated SCTP after 2007. These include RFC 6096 (chunk flag registration), RFC 6335 (IANA port procedures), and RFC 7053 (the SACK-IMMEDIATELY extension). Section 3.35 updates DSCP handling based on newer standards.

The document also clarifies how SCTP responds to soft errors (Section 3.37), handles zero-window probing (Sections 3.20 and 3.39), and processes ICMP for both IPv4 and IPv6 (Section 3.36). No new security considerations are introduced beyond RFC 4960. This is an informational record of fixes that improve robustness and interoperability.
sections.plainLanguage: The document fixes ambiguities and small mistakes without changing SCTP's core design. It also updates SCTP to align with related RFCs that came later. No new security problems are introduced.
